changed: Phase review P-1 (Medium) and P-2 (Low): refs the model writes into a rationale or a citation are now stored and shown as written only when they name something real. Everything else is stored as a jcs-sha256-v1 digest. Details: (1) goal_ref is kept as written only when it is 'run' or the run's task_id@task_version; any other value becomes goal_ref_digest, and there is no #item suffix because AcceptanceSpec has no item ids. (2) Unresolved cited_evidence and rules_considered go to unresolved_evidence_digests and unresolved_rule_digests, which are left out when empty. A KERNEL-* rule id is kept as written only if it is in at_rest.KERNEL_FINDING_IDS, the 27 ids the kernel emits; a drift test checks that set against the source. (3) A citation keeps evidence_id and pointer as written only on a 'named' flag; an unresolved one stores evidence_id_digest and pointer_digest. Citation.pointer is capped at 1024 characters and evidence_id at 128, and the pydantic_ai CITATIONS_SCHEMA mirrors the caps. (4) Persisted findings (validation.completed and the stored continuation) are digest-only, while the model still gets the raw findings through DriverInput, so repair behaviour is unchanged. (5) RationaleRef in contracts/explain.py gains the digest fields (exactly one of goal_ref and goal_ref_digest is set), and explain renders digests labelled as digests. (6) The new kernel module kernel/at_rest.py is registered in the pyproject facade source_modules as a sorted add. Contract acceptance is unchanged apart from the length caps: there is no new refusal and no new repair finding. Commits 24d6878, ad927be and f243991 (R2-2 docstring). Reviews: harness/state/3/reviews/3.R1-r1.json (rework), 3.R1-r2.json (accept).
open_items: The pydantic_ai driver's stored message history (driver state at rest) still holds each raw finding's observed value and the model's own tool-call arguments as written. The owner decides whether driver state is minimised (ADR 0032/0030).
R1-3: ADR 0033 §4 (lines 49 and 59) and target-architecture.md:451 still describe the goal_ref acceptance-item suffix and the old at-rest form verbatim. They are on the owner amendment list.

R2-1: the KERNEL_FINDING_IDS drift test sees only whole string literals. It misses ids built with f-strings or concatenation, of which there are none today; it assumes the dev-install layout; and it scans plugin and adapter modules too. A missed id fails safe, because it is stored as a digest.
cont.rationale and cont.step_rationales keep the full texts in the stored continuation for the approval card (ruling 8, by design).
Events recorded before 24d6878 keep their refs as written, and no migration exists. Only pre-merge branch data is affected.

rulings.ruling: Fix the at-rest and projection boundary, not the contract's acceptance: unresolved refs remain repairs, never refusals, and RefId stays as it is.
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a later contract tightening and an ADR 0033 line

rulings.ruling: The goal_ref closed set is 'run' and task_id@task_version only, with no #item suffix.
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a goal that names an acceptance item is shown only as a digest

rulings.ruling: A citation is stored as written only on a 'named' flag, not on its status (MISMATCHED can be returned before the evidence is looked up).
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a resolved pointer stored as a digest
